title: 1 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 14
description: Ten questions on 1 Corinthians 14: prophesying and other languages, the uncertain trumpet, five words with understanding, and all things done decently and in order.

questions.text: According to verse 2, to whom does he who speaks in another language speak?
questions.explanation: The verse says he speaks not to men, but to God, for no one understands, but in the Spirit he speaks mysteries.

questions.text: What does verse 3 say the one who prophesies speaks to men for?
questions.explanation: The verse says he speaks to men for their edification, exhortation, and consolation.

questions.text: Whom does the one who speaks in another language edify, according to verse 4?
questions.explanation: The verse says he edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the assembly.

questions.text: What question does verse 8 ask about an uncertain trumpet sound?
questions.explanation: The verse asks that if the trumpet gave an uncertain sound, who would prepare himself for war.

answers.text: Who would know the hour of the feast
Who would come together in the assembly
Who would prepare himself for war

questions.text: According to verse 14, what is unfruitful when a man prays in another language?
questions.explanation: The verse says his spirit prays, but his understanding is unfruitful.

questions.text: How many words with his own understanding does the writer say he would rather speak in the assembly?
questions.explanation: Verse 19 says he would rather speak five words with his understanding than ten thousand words in another language.

questions.text: According to verse 22, for whom are other languages a sign?
questions.explanation: The verse says other languages are for a sign, not to those who believe, but to the unbelieving, while prophesying is a sign to those who believe.

questions.text: What does verse 28 say the speaker should do if there is no interpreter?
questions.explanation: The verse says he should keep silent in the assembly, and speak to himself and to God.

answers.text: Speak anyway, since the Spirit speaks mysteries
Keep silent in the assembly and speak to himself and to God
Ask one of the prophets to interpret for him
Leave the assembly at once and pray at home

questions.text: According to verse 29, how many prophets should speak, and what should the others do?
questions.explanation: The verse says, "Let the prophets speak, two or three, and let the others discern."

answers.text: Two or three, and the others should discern
All of them, and the others should keep silent
One only, and the others should interpret
As many as desire, and the others should say nothing

questions.text: How does verse 40 say all things should be done?
questions.explanation: The verse says, "Let all things be done decently and in order."

answers.text: Two or three at a time
